source.title: The Unseen Threat: Residual Knowledge in Machine Unlearning under Perturbed Samples
source.authors: Hsiang Hsu; Pradeep Niroula; Zichang He; Ivan Brugere; Freddy Lécué; C. Chen

record.file_problem: No apparent truncation or garbling; the text includes the main paper and appendices through Appendix C.5.
record.tranche_reason: Tests residual knowledge after unlearning in image classifiers, extending the general unlearning question to a vision setting; it does not test LLM unlearning or the specific attacks named in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The study evaluates image-classification models on perturbed forget samples and compares them with retrained models. These perturbations are not prompt rephrasing, jailbreaks, or other listed LLM attacks, so the reported results do not match a claim version directly. Values used to select hyperparameters are not recorded. C.6 reports per-sample prevalence; C.7 and C.8 report disagreement and perturbed-sample unlearning accuracy at the stated perturbation radius.
record.test_reason: The study covers sample-level unlearning in from-scratch image classifiers (ResNet-18/50, VGG-11 on CIFAR and ImageNet-100). It measures whether Gaussian, FGSM or PGD input perturbations of forget images are still classified correctly more often than by a retrained model. Every claim version concerns LLM knowledge unlearning (WMDP or Harry Potter-style) and LLM attacks: relearning sets, activation ablation, quantization, prompting. So no row measures the named behaviour in the named kind of system. The paper's only link to LLMs is a limitations paragraph calling relearning and jailbreaking 'conceptual parallels'. Its vision result is recorded under fits_no_version rather than as a test.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also prove that disagreement on perturbed forget samples is inevitable in high dimensions even under certified (ε,δ)-unlearning. They frame residual knowledge as a privacy risk across existing image-unlearning methods, and they note a trade-off: larger RURK perturbation radius increases distinguishability.
record.recipe_differences: Image-classification unlearning and Gaussian/adversarial image perturbations; no LLM unlearning recipe or attack from the claim is reproduced.
record.method_sensitivity: Residual knowledge varies with perturbation radius and attack type. The authors report that stronger PGD can reveal residual knowledge at low radii, while increasing the RURK perturbation radius suppresses it more effectively. Results also differ across unlearning methods and datasets.

fits_no_version.finding: Approximate unlearning in image classifiers leaves sample-level residual knowledge. Under small Gaussian perturbations, NTK on Small CIFAR-5 and NGD on CIFAR-10 recognise up to 48% and about 9% of forget samples, respectively, more often than retraining. Original, GD and CF-k stay above 1 in the figures, while GA and SSD over-forget.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In image classifiers, unlearned models re-recognise perturbed variants of forget samples more often than retrained models; the effect grows with perturbation radius for some methods.

fits_no_version.finding: On perturbed forget samples, Original and NTK err less than Re-train, which indicates residual recognition. NGD and RURK err more than Re-train, which is over-forgetting. Fisher roughly matches Re-train at τ=0.0125.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Direction of deviation from retraining on perturbed forget samples varies by image-unlearning method.

record.problems: The experiments are on vision classifiers rather than LLMs and use image perturbations rather than the attacks named in the claim. The main residual-knowledge curves are figure-only; the reported table values cover only selected methods/settings. Several empirical results are based on 3 independent trials, and the text does not give uncertainty for the C.7/C.8 table entries.
record.rows_left_out: Table C.6 values for every tau are included. From Tables C.7 and C.8, only the tau = 0.0125 rows were extracted; other perturbation radii were omitted to keep the record focused and within the row limit. Figure 2 and Figures C.4–C.13 report curves without tabulated values and were not separately extracted.

untested.parts: All parts. There are no LLMs, no hazardous or targeted knowledge benchmark, and no near-chance targeted accuracy criterion. The image methods are judged on gap to a retrained model, not on near-chance accuracy.
All parts. Re-learn time uses the full forget set in image classifiers. There is no small unrelated, loosely related or subset relearning set, and no LLM.
All parts. There is no activation-direction ablation and no access-blocking analysis.
All parts. There is no quantization.
All parts. There is no prompting, rephrasing, jailbreak, language or in-context attack. The input perturbations are pixel-level noise or adversarial attacks on images.
All parts. RURK is a robust-unlearning method for image classifiers against input perturbations, not evaluated against LLM attacks.

missing.what: Re-learn time (epochs to re-acquire the forget set) for all methods, e.g. NegGrad+ 1.00 vs Re-train 17.33 on CIFAR-10. This is a fine-tuning recovery measure, though on image classifiers with the full forget set, so it does not match version B.
Residual-knowledge curves for all methods under Gaussian, FGSM and PGD, including ImageNet-100. These are the main result but are figure-only.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from the reader's 'tests'/T3 to 'discusses'/T6. The domain (from-scratch image classifiers, sample unlearning, pixel perturbations) differs in kind of system and attack from every version, which all concern LLM knowledge unlearning. No labels are given. The study is not an original source. Several C7/C8 row states were corrected because disagreement is non-directional and because higher-than-retrain unlearn accuracy indicates over-forgetting (reversed relative to residual knowledge), not absence.

versions.untested_parts: No LLMs or listed LLM attacks; the image methods generally do not establish the version’s condition of near-chance targeted accuracy while preserving general ability.
Re-learn time is reported, but not recovery from a small set of unrelated, loosely related, or subset-of-facts training examples as specified.
No activation-direction ablation or test of an internal access-blocking mechanism.
No prompt rephrasing, jailbreak, language variation, or in-context information attack; the study instead perturbs image inputs.
RURK addresses image-model residual knowledge under image perturbations, not resistance to the attacks specified in the claim.

rows.note: The study defines unlearning accuracy as 1 minus forget accuracy.
rows.check: Unlearn accuracy on perturbed forget samples is 0.5014 against Re-train 0.1478. NGD misclassifies far more perturbed forget samples than retraining, which is over-forgetting, the opposite of residual knowledge. 'absent' understates this.

rows.note: The study defines unlearning accuracy as 1 minus forget accuracy.
rows.check: 0.2330 against Re-train 0.1478. RURK misclassifies more perturbed forget samples than retraining, which is the opposite of residual recognition. It is also the study's own method compared with baselines.
